research_scope: Source-free first-pass scan of twelve existing formulations, no new mathematical definitions or external references.

items.review_rationale: Read invertibility of a monoidal object, distinguished the linked monoidal-category unit from a potentially separate tensor-inverse witness, without researching external terminology.

references.matching_note: X and Y are objects of the existing monoidal-category context.

references.context: Category theory: two-sided tensor inverse of an object up to monoidal isomorphism
references.reason: Tensoring and isomorphism are supplied by the monoidal structure, but the inverse-witness construction is a candidate for global comparison.

references.disposition: Unit object is inherent in the linked monoidal category rather than an independent new definition in this formulation.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the full ind-object filtered-diagram splitting and eventual stabilization clauses, linked filtered indexing and cocones, and saved split arrows, ind-object and eventual equality as occurrence-only.

references.matching_note: The indexing category is filtered.
The cocone has the categorical colimit form, although X is not assumed to be the colimit.

references.context: Category theory: section/retraction pair of arrows for a filtered diagram stage and cocone
references.reason: The stage map exhibits a splitting and should be compared with other split-arrow occurrences.

references.phrase: maps into a later common stage eventually agree
references.context: Category theory: eventual equality of arrows in filtered diagrams
references.reason: Eventual identification of maps after transition functors is characteristic of ind-object constructions.

references.context: Category theory: formal filtered-colimit object of a category
references.reason: The term is named in the definition heading and may need a separate contextual meaning; do not source-research it now.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the dual pro-object cofiltered-diagram criterion, preserving arrow direction, cone and stage maps and the difference from ind-objects.

references.matching_note: The indexing shape is a cofiltered category.
The cone is shaped like a categorical inverse limit cone, without assuming a limit.

references.context: Category theory: retraction/section pair of arrows for a cofiltered pro-object diagram
references.reason: The chosen stage retracts through X in a specified direction, distinct from the ind case.

references.context: Category theory: eventual factorization of inverse diagram transition arrows through a chosen object
references.reason: This pro-object condition uses a common earlier stage and should be pooled with other pro-diagram occurrences.

references.context: Category theory: formal cofiltered inverse diagram regarded as an object of a pro-category
references.reason: The meaning is not automatically the same as an ordinary inverse limit object.

items.review_rationale: Read the complete characteristic-polynomial matrix definition, distinguishing determinant, square matrix, polynomial ring and matrix identity from the unrelated characteristic of a field.

references.phrase: n×n matrix A over a commutative ring R
references.context: Linear algebra: finite square matrix of elements of a commutative ring
references.reason: A square matrix is a distinct object from the adjacency matrix of a graph; do not mislink it.

references.context: Linear algebra: determinant of a square matrix of polynomial entries
references.reason: The determinant is an algebraic construction over the polynomial ring R[t].

references.context: Commutative algebra: polynomial ring in one indeterminate over a commutative unital ring
references.reason: Distinguish the coefficient polynomial ring from a general ring and from an indexed polynomial algebra.

references.context: Linear algebra: n-by-n identity matrix with diagonal units and off-diagonal zeros
references.reason: This is a specific linear algebra identity, rather than an arbitrary group identity.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed smoothness of a commutative ring map using existing ring finite presentation, relative naive cotangent complex and finite projective module, retaining homological quasi-isomorphism and degree support.

references.matching_note: The source and target are commutative unital rings with a unital ring map.
Finite presentation here is the ring-map/R-algebra sense, not module finite presentation.
The complex is explicitly the relative naive cotangent complex of the ring map.
The target comparison object is finite projective as an S-module.

references.phrase: quasi-isomorphic to a finite projective S-module
references.context: Homological algebra: quasi-isomorphism of complexes inducing isomorphisms on homology
references.reason: A quasi-isomorphism is a homological-algebra notion, not mere isomorphism of modules.

references.context: Homological algebra: chain complex concentrated in degree zero
references.reason: This is a degree-support condition on the comparison complex.

items.review_rationale: Read locally closed immersion as factorization of an existing scheme morphism into closed and open immersions, without introducing unrelated immersion terminology.

references.matching_note: The ambient morphism is a scheme morphism.
The first factor is an immersion that is closed in the appropriate scheme/locally-ringed-space sense.
The second factor is an open immersion of schemes regarded as locally ringed spaces.

references.phrase: factorization through a closed immersion followed by an open immersion
references.disposition: The existence of the two-factor factorization is the defining property of a locally closed immersion, not an independent missing word.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the binary coproduct universal property, preserving arbitrary-category size convention and saving canonical injections and unique mediating arrows.

references.context: Category theory: potentially large category with objects and arrows
references.reason: The existing generic category meaning explicitly assumes smallness, not warranted here.

references.context: Category theory: pair of arrows into the coproduct object from two objects
references.reason: These are canonical coproduct injections with source objects X,Y.

references.context: Category theory: universal mediating morphism out of a binary coproduct
references.reason: The unique factorization is the universal property of the coproduct cocone.

references.disposition: Composition equations are already ordinary operations in the ambient category.

items.review_rationale: Read catenarity as the equal-length condition on maximal chains of nested irreducible closed subspaces and linked topology and codimension in the correct contexts.

references.matching_note: Catenary space is an arbitrary topological space.
An irreducible closed subset has the irreducibility property in its subspace topology.
The codimension is the chain-length invariant for nested irreducible closed subspaces.

references.phrase: maximal chains of irreducible closed subsets
references.context: Topology: maximal strictly nested chains of irreducible closed subsets between Y and Z
references.reason: The maximal-chain condition is a poset concept and should be compared with other chain contexts.

references.phrase: all maximal chains have the same finite length
references.disposition: This equal-length requirement constitutes the catenary property rather than a separate named prerequisite.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed topological codimension as supremum of lengths of nested irreducible closed subsets, distinguishing set-theoretic strict inclusion and irreducibility.

references.matching_note: Codimension is defined in an arbitrary topological space.
Y is irreducible in its subspace topology.
The inclusions are proper, nested subset inclusions.

references.context: Topology: irreducible closed subsets of a common ambient topological space X
references.reason: The irreducible-subspace meaning needs the closed-subset condition checked in the shared ambient space.

references.disposition: The definition directly takes a least upper bound of finite chain lengths.

items.review_rationale: Read the integrally closed domain property in its fraction field, linking the domain, fraction field and integrality polynomial criterion while recording integral-closure terminology.

references.matching_note: The starting ring is an integral domain under the nonzero unital convention.
Fraction field supplies the overfield containing elements integral over R.

references.phrase: monic polynomial with coefficients in R
references.matching_note: The polynomial relation in the fraction field is the existing integral-element-over-R property.

references.phrase: every element integral over R already belongs to R
references.context: Commutative algebra: integral closure of an integral domain inside its fraction field
references.reason: The defining integrally-closed property is contextual and may match a separately indexed integral-closure meaning.

references.disposition: Ordinary containment in the base ring is used as the condition, not a new mathematical object.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed normal commutative ring by localization at primes, recognizing integral-domain normality on each local ring and preserving the distinct scope of normal rings and normal domains.

references.matching_note: The commutative-unital ring convention is implicit; the ring-map meaning is a contextual proxy, not a complete commutative ring definition.
Localize at the multiplicative complement of prime p.
The localization is indexed by prime ideals of R.
The localized ring is required to satisfy the indexed normal/integrally-closed domain property.
Integrally closed domain refers to its fraction field.

items.review_rationale: Read fibred-in-sets condition as a fibred-in-groupoids category with discrete fibres, preserving fibre-of-functor terminology and avoiding an unsupported small-category requirement.

references.matching_note: A fibred category with groupoid fibres is the immediate parent meaning.
Every fibre E_U is discrete, with only identity arrows.

references.context: Category theory: functor p from a category E to a base category C
references.reason: Unqualified category/functor need not be small; preserve the contextual source wording.

references.context: Category theory: fibre of a functor p:E→C over an object U
references.reason: The fibre is the subcategory of objects and arrows lying over the identity of U.
